summary: The Power Plant Reliability Act of 2025 amends the Federal Power Act to let FERC order continued operation of electric generating units (with compensation and cost allocation) when interstate service is or will soon be inadequate, while requiring owners of units of 5+ MW on the bulk-power system to give at least five years' advance notice before planned retirement.

scores.thoughts: The bill empowers FERC to issue orders requiring continued operation of generating units and to set rates/charges for compensation, but these are borne by utilities and ratepayers rather than direct federal appropriations or spending. No expansion or reduction of government budgets is involved.
The legislation contains no provisions related to taxes, tax rates, credits, or revenue collection.
No connection to healthcare policy, insurance, or medical services.
Completely unrelated to firearms or gun regulations.
No provisions addressing immigration, borders, or visas.
No relevance to reproductive rights or abortion access.
No impact on military budgets or defense policy.

Section 207(a)(5) explicitly shields utilities from liability under federal, state, or local environmental laws when complying with FERC orders to keep generating units operating. This directly weakens environmental protections to prioritize grid reliability.
No provisions affecting welfare programs, food assistance, or social benefits.
